ls.summary: Lists files and directories in the current (or given) location.

flags.-l: long format - shows permissions, owner, size, date
flags.-a: show hidden files (those starting with a dot)

cd.summary: Changes your current directory (where you 'are' in the filesystem).

flags.-: go back to the previous directory
flags.~: shortcut for your home directory (used as an argument, e.g. cd ~)

pwd.summary: Prints the full path of the directory you're currently in.

flags.-p: create parent directories as needed (no error if they already exist)

rmdir.summary: Removes an EMPTY directory. Fails if it has anything inside.

rm.summary: Deletes files (or directories with -r). This does NOT go to a trash bin - it's permanent.

flags.-r: delete directories and their contents recursively
flags.-f: force - skip confirmation prompts, ignore nonexistent files
flags.-i: ask for confirmation before each deletion (safer)

rm.danger: rm -rf can permanently delete entire directory trees with no undo. Always double-check the path.

flags.-i: ask before overwriting an existing file

mv.summary: Moves or renames files/directories. There's no separate 'rename' command - mv does both.

flags.-i: ask before overwriting an existing file

touch.summary: Creates an empty file if it doesn't exist, or updates its timestamp if it does.

cat.summary: Prints a file's entire contents to the screen. Good for short files.

less.summary: Views a file one screen at a time - better than cat for long files. Press 'q' to quit.

head.summary: Shows the first lines of a file (default: 10).

flags.-n: number of lines to show, e.g. -n 20

tail.summary: Shows the last lines of a file (default: 10). Great for checking recent log entries.

flags.-f: follow the file live as new lines are added

grep.summary: Searches text for lines matching a pattern.

flags.-v: invert match - show lines that DON'T match

find.summary: Searches for files/directories by name, type, size, or other criteria.

flags.-type: match by type: f for file, d for directory

chmod.summary: Changes a file's permissions (who can read/write/execute it).

flags.-R: apply recursively to a directory and its contents

chmod.danger: chmod -R on system directories (like /) can break your OS. Only use -R inside your own project folders.

chown.summary: Changes who owns a file (user and/or group). Usually needs sudo.

flags.aux: show all processes from all users, in detailed format

kill.summary: Sends a signal to a process, usually to stop it. Needs the process ID (PID) from ps.

flags.-9: force-kill immediately (last resort, skips graceful shutdown)

top.summary: Shows a live, updating view of running processes and resource usage. Press 'q' to quit.

df.summary: Shows disk space usage for mounted filesystems.

du.summary: Shows how much disk space files/directories are using.

flags.-s: summarize - show a total instead of every subfile

man.summary: Opens the manual page for a command - the official, detailed documentation. Press 'q' to quit.

sudo.summary: Runs a command with administrator (root) privileges. Use carefully - it can change or break anything on the system.
sudo.danger: Commands run with sudo bypass normal safety checks. Never run something with sudo unless you understand what it does.

apt.summary: Package manager for Debian/Ubuntu-based systems - installs, updates, and removes software.

flags.update: refresh the list of available packages
flags.install: install a package, e.g. apt install curl

echo.summary: Prints text to the screen. Often used to check variable values or write into files.

export.summary: Sets an environment variable that's visible to programs you run afterward in this shell session.

history.summary: Shows a list of commands you've previously run in the shell.

wc.summary: Counts lines, words, or characters in a file or input.

tar.summary: Archives (bundles) files together, optionally with compression.

flags.-f: specify the archive filename (usually last flag before the filename)

curl.summary: Transfers data to/from a URL - commonly used to test APIs or download files.

flags.-O: save output to a file named like the remote file
flags.-X: specify the HTTP method, e.g. -X POST

ssh.summary: Connects securely to a remote machine's shell over the network.

scp.summary: Copies files between machines over SSH.

git.summary: Version control tool for tracking changes to code over time.

flags.status: show what's changed since the last commit
flags.add: stage changes for the next commit
flags.commit: save staged changes with a message
flags.push: upload commits to a remote repository
flags.pull: download and merge changes from a remote repository

python3.summary: Runs the Python 3 interpreter, either interactively or on a script file.

flags.-m: run a library module as a script

alias.summary: Creates a shortcut name for a longer command.

which.summary: Shows the full path of the program that would run for a given command name.

diff.summary: Compares two files and shows the differences between them.

flags.-u: unified format (easier to read, standard for patches)

ln.summary: Creates a link to a file. Symbolic links act like shortcuts.

whoami.summary: Prints the username you're currently logged in as.

uname.summary: Prints system information like the OS kernel name and version.
